Seen things other people couldn’t see? I don’t think so… not in the way I think you mean, like seeing a person standing there who isn’t there, or objects moving around, or something like that.

I mean… not really outside of that, no. This is the thing. People try to make it sound like I have all these strange beliefs about everything, but I don’t. Unusually high or euphoric? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m worked up, definitely, but I wouldn’t call it “high” or like I’m on top of the world or anything. It’s more like I’m frustrated, or tense, or trying to keep up with everything that’s happening.

That’s why I came in.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe anyone is controlling your thoughts or putting thoughts into your mind?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. I mean, that’s not really how it feels to me. My thoughts feel like my thoughts. I’m not sitting there thinking someone is, like, inserting words into my head or moving my mind around like a remote control or something.\n\nWhat I’m saying is more that people are influencing what happens around me, or trying to pressure me, or setting things up so I’ll react a certain way. That’s different. I know what I think, and I know when I’m thinking it. I just also know there are things going on outside of me that don’t add up. But no, I wouldn’t say anyone is controlling my thoughts or putting thoughts into my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. Not voices like someone talking when nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes I’ll hear normal things — a car outside, someone in the hallway, the neighbors, things like that — and I might pay closer attention than I used to because of everything going on. But I’m not hearing, like, voices speaking to me out of nowhere.\n\nIf I’m stressed or tired, I might replay conversations in my head, like what someone said or how they said it, and I’ll think about it over and over. But that’s still me thinking about it. It’s not like there’s some person I can hear talking to me when no one is there. So… no, I wouldn’t describe it that way.\n\nDoctor: Have you had a time when you felt unusually energetic or wired for days in a row and needed much less sleep than usual?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I’ve definitely had times where I stayed up too late, or where I was tense and couldn’t settle down because I had a lot on my mind, but that’s not the same as feeling like I had all this extra energy and didn’t need sleep.\n\nIf anything, when I don’t sleep, I feel it. I get worn down. I might keep going because I have to — work, dealing with things, trying to keep up — but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly wired for days and fine on barely any sleep. I don’t remember a stretch like that where I felt unusually energized or unstoppable or anything.\n\nDoctor: For at least one month, have you continuously believed that people were working together to push you out of your house?\n\nPatient: Yes. More than a month. It’s been… honestly, close to two years that I’ve been seeing it happen.\n\nAnd I know how that sounds, because everyone keeps trying to make it sound like it’s just foreclosure paperwork, or missed payments, or some mistake with the loan servicer, like if they put enough documents in front of me I’m supposed to just accept their version of it. But I don’t. Because it’s not just one thing. It’s the bank, the loan servicer, and then things happening around my job too, like people suddenly acting differently, little comments, timing of things, pressure from different directions. It all lines up too neatly.\n\nSo yes, I have believed continuously that people are working together to push me out of my house. Not for a week, not just when I was upset — this has been going on for a long time, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes.\n\nDoctor: Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I felt really low or weighed down, but I don’t know if I would say “depressed most of the day nearly every day” for two straight weeks. That sounds very specific, and I don’t want to say yes if that’s not really what it was.\n\nThere have definitely been times where I was upset and worn out by everything, and I didn’t feel like myself, but I don’t always track it day by day like that. Some days I could still get up and do what I needed to do, even if I felt bad underneath it. Other days it felt heavier. So… I guess I’d say I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear two-week period in mind where I can confidently say yes, that was happening nearly every day.\n\nDoctor: Has anyone told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?\n\nPatient: I don’t think anyone has said it to me that way, no. I mean, people have told me I “go on too long” sometimes, or that I’m giving too much background, but that’s different from saying I don’t make sense.\n\nSometimes I feel like if I don’t explain the whole chain of events, then people take one little piece out of context and act like it means something else. So I might circle back or add details, but in my mind it’s connected. It’s not like I’m just jumping randomly from one thing to another.\n\nSo… no, I don’t think anyone has told me my speech is hard to follow in that way. Maybe they get impatient, but that’s not the same thing.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed that you’ve become less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: I don’t know if I’d call it “less interested” exactly. I mean, I still like the same things in theory. If you asked me, do I like seeing certain people, do I like going out for coffee, watching a show, walking around stores, things like that — yes, I do.\n\nBut lately I guess I don’t always feel like dealing with people as much. Sometimes it feels like too much effort to explain myself, or to sit there pretending everything is normal when it isn’t. So I may say no to things more often, but I don’t know if that’s because I lost interest in them, or because I’m tired and don’t want the conversation to turn into people questioning me or acting like they know better.\n\nSo… I haven’t noticed it as a clear “I don’t enjoy anything anymore” kind of thing. It’s more complicated than that. I still want to do things sometimes, just not always with the same energy, and not if I feel like I’m going to have to manage everyone else’s reactions.\n\nDoctor: Have you seen things that other people could not see?\n\nPatient: Seen things other people couldn’t see? I don’t think so… not in the way I think you mean, like seeing a person standing there who isn’t there, or objects moving around, or something like that.\n\nI mean, sometimes I notice things other people miss, like a look someone gives, or a car that’s been around more than once, or little things that don’t seem accidental to me. But that’s not really “seeing things” like a vision or hallucination, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s more that I’m paying attention and other people act like they don’t notice, or they dismiss it.\n\nSo no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things that weren’t there. At least not that I can think of.\n\nDoctor: Outside of this situation with your house and the people you believe are involved, do you have any other beliefs that others say are not true or hard to believe?\n\nPatient: I mean… not really outside of that, no. This is the thing. People try to make it sound like I have all these strange beliefs about everything, but I don’t. I go to work, I do my job, I deal with customers, schedules, inventory, all of that. I’m not walking around thinking every random person is involved in something.\n\nBut with the house, with the foreclosure, with the bank and the loan servicer and the way certain people at work started acting around the same time… that’s different. That’s not just me “believing something hard to believe.” That’s me seeing a pattern over and over for almost two years and then everyone telling me it’s just paperwork or missed payments or some misunderstanding. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing, because the papers don’t explain the timing, or the way information seems to get around, or how people suddenly know things they shouldn’t.\n\nSo if you’re asking whether there are other things like that, no, I wouldn’t say so. It’s this situation. But I don’t accept that it’s not true just because other people don’t want to admit it.\n\nDoctor: During the time this has been going on, have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or excessively irritable?\n\nPatient: Unusually high or euphoric? Irritable maybe at times, but not out of nowhere.\n\nDoctor: Aside from the problems related to your house, have you been able to function normally at work and in your daily life?\n\nPatient: Yes… I mean, mostly, when it’s not touching the house situation, I can function. I’m not just sitting at home unable to do anything.\n\nAnd I take care of myself, too. I get dressed, I keep up with basic things, I run errands. It’s just that this situation keeps intruding, especially when something reminds me of it or seems connected.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt someone touching your body when no one was there?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. That’s kind of the thing people don’t understand. I’ve definitely been upset, and worn down, and sometimes it feels like this whole thing is sitting on my chest all the time, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being depressed in the way you mean.\n\nThere are days where I’m angry more than sad. Or scared. Or just exhausted from thinking about it. I’ve had bad stretches, yes, but I don’t know that I’d say I felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day. It feels more tied to what’s happening and what it means for my house than like a constant depression on its own.\n\nDoctor: Has there ever been a full month when you had these beliefs about people working against you, but were not feeling depressed or unusually high during that time?\n\nPatient: Yes. I mean, yes, there’s definitely been more than a full month where I believed people were working against me and I wasn’t depressed or “high” or anything like that.\n\nThat’s kind of the thing people don’t understand.
